findings.title: T-07 orphan descendants — mitigation now effective (re-confirmed at HEAD b503b590)
findings.description: Re-hunt at HEAD b503b590: runner._reap_after_kill now uses os.killpg on a process group owned by the child (placed in its own session via start_new_session=True on the create_subprocess_exec call). The previous hunt's finding (commit a4a6bc5) is verified resolved — code-level fix is in place and the repro tests in test_bug_hunt_resolutions.py pass.
findings.reasoning: Verification at current HEAD: (1) grep -n 'start_new_session=True' runner.py returns line 509 — Popen creates a new session so killpg targets only the child group, never the runner. (2) _reap_after_kill (lines 360-391) compares child_pgid vs my_pgid (os.getpgid(0)) and falls back to proc.kill() if they match (defensive — protects against direct-invocation paths that didn't set start_new_session). (3) pytest test_bug_hunt_resolutions.py::test_t07_no_orphan_descendant_after_timeout PASSED — spawns `python3 -c 'import subprocess,time; subprocess.Popen(["sleep","30"]); time.sleep(15)'` via run_task(timeout_seconds=3) and asserts no descendant PID remains. Mitigation is effective.
findings.suggested_fix: No further action — fix is in place and verified.
findings.verify_evidence: runner.py:509 sets start_new_session=True; runner.py:360-391 uses killpg with my_pgid guard; 8/8 tests in test_bug_hunt_resolutions.py pass including test_t07_no_orphan_descendant_after_timeout.
findings.attack_vector: T-07: Long-running task killed by SIGKILL leaves descendant processes running as orphans (reparented to launchd/init). Each submission leaks a new long-lived process.
findings.attempted_exploit: Submit task with command='python3 -c "import subprocess,time; subprocess.Popen(['sleep','3600']); time.sleep(600)"' and timeout=3s. Pre-fix: descendant sleep survives with PPID=1. Post-fix (current HEAD): killpg(child_pgid, SIGKILL) terminates the entire process group rooted at the child; no orphan PID remains.

findings.title: T-01 spoofing — mitigation effective (constant-time compare + plaintext-never-stored)
findings.description: Re-hunt at HEAD b503b590: auth.compare_keys uses hmac.compare_digest per NFR-02; auth.hash_key stores only the 64-char SHA-256 hex; the X-API-Key header is never persisted (only its digest hits key_repo.find_by_hash). Forged key cannot bypass via timing oracle or hash collision.
findings.reasoning: Verification: hmac.compare_digest is the standard constant-time primitive (PEP 207) — invariant time regardless of byte mismatches. hash_key is SHA-256 hexdigest; 64-char output, 256-bit collision resistance. Empty-string inputs return False without invoking compare_digest (line 91-92 — uniform 401). Forged X-API-Key with arbitrary plaintext: hash mismatch → find_by_hash returns None → 401 unauthenticated (deps.py:317-322). No naive == on key material anywhere in source. test_keys_hashed_and_compared_with_hmac_compare_digest PASSES.
findings.verify_evidence: auth.py:91 — hmac.compare_digest is the only comparator. auth.py:75 — SHA-256 hexdigest (no plaintext). deps.py:317 — key_repo.find_by_hash uses the digest as the lookup key.

resolution.refute_evidence: T-01 mitigation is in place: auth.py:91 uses hmac.compare_digest (constant-time), auth.py:75 uses hashlib.sha256 (no plaintext persisted), deps.py:317 looks up by hash. test_keys_hashed_and_compared_with_hmac_compare_digest in test_nfr_patterns.py PASSED — grep confirms hmac.compare_digest as the only credential comparator. Forged key attack is blocked.

findings.attack_vector: T-01: Attacker presents a forged X-API-Key header to impersonate a legitimate client.
findings.attempted_exploit: Submit GET /v1/tasks with arbitrary X-API-Key value (e.g. 'fake-key-12345'). Expected outcome: 401 unauthenticated. Verified by inspection: key_repo.find_by_hash(hash_key('fake-key-12345')) returns None (no row keyed by that digest), deps.py:318-319 raises _unauthorized('invalid X-API-Key').

findings.title: T-02 tampering — mitigation effective (Pydantic validation + parameterised persistence)
findings.description: Re-hunt at HEAD b503b590: TaskCreate._no_injection_chars rejects the full shell-metachar blacklist (lines 22, 38-46 of schemas.py); Field max_length=1000 caps command length; task_repo.create takes a dict and never concatenates user input into SQL (production uses SQLAlchemy ORM parameter binding); HTTPException(422) on ValueError from the repo (tasks.py:71-74) prevents malformed rows from leaking into the persistence layer.
findings.reasoning: Verification: (1) schemas.py:22 — _INJECTION_CHARS = set(";|&`$()<>\n") — full SPEC §3 FR-01 blacklist. (2) schemas.py:35 — Field(max_length=1000) caps command at 1KB. (3) tasks.py:64 — command passed via dict, no string concatenation; SQLAlchemy ORM (when wired) uses parameter binding. (4) tasks.py:67-74 — ValueError mapped to 422 so invalid rows don't get into the repo. (5) The runner also tokenises via shlex.split (runner.py:480) and uses create_subprocess_exec(*args) with shell=False (runner.py:505-510) — defence in depth. test_no_string_concat_sql_in_source PASSED.
findings.verify_evidence: schemas.py:22 injection-char blacklist; schemas.py:35 max_length=1000; tasks.py:64 dict-passing create (no SQL concat); tasks.py:67-74 ValueError → 422; runner.py:480 shlex.split; runner.py:505-510 shell=False exec.

resolution.refute_evidence: T-02 mitigation is in place across layers: schemas.py:22 (injection-char blacklist), schemas.py:35 (max_length=1000), tasks.py:64 (dict-based create; no SQL string concat), runner.py:480 (shlex.split), runner.py:505-510 (shell=False + start_new_session=True). test_no_string_concat_sql_in_source PASSED. Malformed body attack is blocked at validation.

findings.attack_vector: T-02: Malformed task body (oversize name, control chars, SQL fragments) corrupts persisted state or is logged unsafely.
findings.attempted_exploit: Submit POST /v1/tasks with body={'command': 'echo x; rm -rf /', 'name': 'x'} — schema validation raises ValueError('forbidden characters: ;') → 422. Body with command > 1000 chars → Pydantic max_length violation → 422. Body with SQL concatenation patterns → passed as parameter to SQLAlchemy (no string concat) → executed as parameterised statement.

findings.title: T-03 elevation_of_privilege — mitigation effective (scope-rank check denies read → admin)
findings.description: Re-hunt at HEAD b503b590: DELETE /v1/tasks/{id} declares dependencies=[_require_admin] (tasks.py:138); auth.scope_satisfies('read', 'admin') returns False because _SCOPE_RANK['read']=0 < _SCOPE_RANK['admin']=2 (auth.py:28, 60-64). A read-scope key cannot invoke the admin-only endpoint.
findings.reasoning: Verification: tasks.py:138 binds the DELETE handler to _require_admin (line 42). _require_admin wraps _dependency which calls scope_satisfies(granted, 'admin'). _SCOPE_RANK['read']=0; _SCOPE_RANK['admin']=2; 0 >= 2 is False → raises _forbidden('admin'). 403 problem+json body returned. No other code path bypasses this (no manual scope check elsewhere; require_api_key returns the principal as dict and require_scope is the only enforcement). FR-04 AC-4.2 satisfied.
findings.verify_evidence: tasks.py:138 dependencies=[_require_admin]; deps.py:385 scope_satisfies(granted, scope); auth.py:28 _SCOPE_RANK = {read:0, write:1, admin:2}; auth.py:60-64 deny-by-default (unknown scope → -1 → False).

resolution.refute_evidence: T-03 mitigation is in place: tasks.py:138 binds DELETE to _require_admin; deps.py:385 invokes scope_satisfies; auth.py:60-64 returns False when granted_rank < required_rank. Read-scope token cannot invoke DELETE /v1/tasks/{id}. test_403_body_does_not_leak_resource_existence PASSED (related contract).

findings.attack_vector: T-03: Token with 'read' scope successfully invokes 'admin'-only DELETE /v1/tasks/{id}.
findings.attempted_exploit: Send DELETE /v1/tasks/{some_id} with X-API-Key of a read-scope token. Expected outcome: 403 forbidden (insufficient scope). Verified by inspection: tasks.py:138 binds _require_admin; deps.py:385 scope_satisfies('read', 'admin') returns False; deps.py:386 raises _forbidden('admin'); HTTPException(403, type=/errors/forbidden).

findings.title: T-04 information_disclosure — mitigation effective (403 body does not leak resource existence)
findings.description: Re-hunt at HEAD b503b590: _forbidden (deps.py:234-262) returns a generic 'insufficient scope' detail string with only 'required_scope' (a permission level, NOT a resource id). The 403 body shape is identical regardless of whether the underlying resource exists or not — caller cannot enumerate.
findings.reasoning: Verification: deps.py:253-256 detail string contains no resource id, no 'not found' phrase, no 'exists'/'missing' distinction. deps.py:260 — required_scope is the *requested* scope (e.g. 'admin'), not the resource. Compare with the 404 path (tasks.py:97-99 — GET /v1/tasks/{id} returns 404 with 'task {task_id} not found') — these are distinct routes with distinct response shapes. A caller probing for resource existence via DELETE /v1/tasks/{id} (admin-gated) cannot distinguish 'admin scope required but missing' from 'resource exists' because the 403 detail never references the resource id. test_403_body_does_not_leak_resource_existence PASSED.
findings.verify_evidence: deps.py:253-256 generic detail string (no resource id, no not-found phrase); deps.py:260 required_scope is a permission level not an identifier.

resolution.refute_evidence: T-04 mitigation is in place: deps.py:253-256 detail string is 'insufficient scope: requested scope is not granted by the presented API key' (no resource id, no existence hint); deps.py:260 emits 'required_scope' (a permission level, not a resource). test_403_body_does_not_leak_resource_existence PASSED — confirms the 403 body is invariant to resource existence.

findings.attack_vector: T-04: 403 response body reveals whether a task id exists, enabling enumeration of internal state.
findings.attempted_exploit: Send DELETE /v1/tasks/{probe_id} with a write-scope (not admin) key. Expected outcome: 403 forbidden with body containing only {type, title, status, detail, required_scope} — no reference to probe_id. Verified by inspection: deps.py:253-256 detail is generic; deps.py:260 required_scope='admin' is identical for any probe_id.

findings.title: T-05 tampering — mitigation effective (parameterised SQL via SQLAlchemy ORM)
findings.description: Re-hunt at HEAD b503b590: every query against the tasks table goes through SQLAlchemy ORM or textual select() with bound parameters (task_repo.py uses SQLAlchemy ORM via session_scope + orm.Task; rate_repo.py uses select(...).where(...).with_for_update()). No f-string or string-concatenation SQL exists in the source tree.
findings.reasoning: Verification: (1) in-memory fake (task_repo.py:38-54) does dict lookups, no SQL. (2) production orm (orm.py — uses Mapped[] mapped_column) and rate_repo (lines 117, 157 — select(...).where(...)) use parameter binding. (3) session.py:158-160 — session.execute(delete(Tag)) uses parameter binding. (4) test_no_string_concat_sql_in_source scans the entire source tree for SQL string concat patterns and PASSES. (5) bandit scan (test_bandit_zero_high_zero_medium) finds 0 HIGH/MEDIUM — SQL injection is the primary bandit B608 check.
findings.verify_evidence: task_repo.py:42 dict-based duplicate check; rate_repo.py:117, 157 select(...).where(...); session.py:158-160 session.execute(delete(...)). No raw SQL strings.

resolution.refute_evidence: T-05 mitigation is in place: rate_repo.py:117 and 157 use SQLAlchemy select(...).where(...) with parameter binding; session.py:158-160 use session.execute(delete(...)); task_repo.py:38-54 uses dict lookups (no SQL at all). test_no_string_concat_sql_in_source PASSED (zero f-string/format SQL in source); test_bandit_zero_high_zero_medium PASSED (Bandit B608 + B610 = 0). SQL injection is blocked.

findings.attack_vector: T-05: SQL injection via string concatenation reaches the database.
findings.attempted_exploit: Submit task with command containing "'; DROP TABLE tasks; --". Expected outcome: command rejected at schema validation (schemas.py:22 — semicolon in _INJECTION_CHARS) → 422. Even if accepted, command is stored as a Python string parameter via SQLAlchemy ORM (no SQL parse), and the runner spawns via create_subprocess_exec (no shell interpretation).

findings.title: T-06 elevation_of_privilege — mitigation effective (shlex.split + shell=False exec)
findings.description: Re-hunt at HEAD b503b590: runner.run_task tokenises command with shlex.split (runner.py:480) and spawns via asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(*args) with shell=False (the default; runner.py:505-510). The child runs as a direct exec of argv[0] with no shell interpretation — no metachar escape possible.
findings.reasoning: Verification: (1) runner.py:480 — shlex.split tokenises safely (no shell substitution). (2) runner.py:505-510 — asyncio.create_subprocess_exec with *args splat means each token becomes an argv element; the kernel's execve is invoked directly with no /bin/sh -c interpolation. (3) start_new_session=True (line 509) only affects process-group placement for killpg, not shell interpretation. (4) schemas.py:22 pre-filters the most dangerous chars (defence in depth). (5) test_no_shell_true_eval_exec_in_source PASSED — grep confirms no shell=True or eval/exec in source.
findings.verify_evidence: runner.py:480 shlex.split; runner.py:505-510 create_subprocess_exec(*args, shell=default-False); schemas.py:22 pre-filter.

resolution.refute_evidence: T-06 mitigation is in place: runner.py:480 uses shlex.split (safe POSIX tokenisation); runner.py:505-510 uses asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(*args) with shell implicitly False. The exec'd child is a direct argv exec, no shell interpretation. test_no_shell_true_eval_exec_in_source PASSED — grep over source tree confirms zero shell=True / eval / exec calls. Shell-metachar injection is blocked at exec time.

findings.attack_vector: T-06: Attacker injects shell metacharacters via the task command field, escaping the intended command.
findings.attempted_exploit: Submit task command='echo hello; cat /etc/passwd'. Schema validation (schemas.py:22) rejects the semicolon → 422. Even bypassing schema, shlex.split produces ['echo', 'hello;', 'cat', '/etc/passwd'] (4 args) and exec'd as a single argv — the semicolon is just a character in argv[1], not a shell operator. No shell ever runs.

findings.title: T-09 repudiation — mitigation effective (correlation_id in body + header + log)
findings.description: Re-hunt at HEAD b503b590: app._problem_response generates correlation_id (uuid4 hex) and includes it in (a) the problem+json body field 'correlation_id' (errors.py:120-127), (b) the X-Correlation-Id response header (app.py:115), and (c) a server-side WARNING log line (app.py:106-112). Inbound X-Correlation-Id header is honoured (app.py:73-76) so upstream proxies can stitch the trace end-to-end.
findings.reasoning: Verification: errors.py:115-127 emits correlation_id in body. app.py:73-76 honours inbound X-Correlation-Id header (upstream stitching). app.py:106-112 logs WARNING with the same correlation_id. app.py:115 sets X-Correlation-Id response header. All four handlers (RequestValidationError, HTTPException, generic Exception, plus the body pre-validation middleware) route through _problem_response (app.py:271-321, 180-187). Even internal 500s carry correlation_id so destructive actions cannot be repudiated. test_no_bare_except_or_except_exception_pass + test_error_body_no_stack_sql_or_paths PASS.
findings.verify_evidence: errors.py:115-127 correlation_id in body; app.py:73-76 inbound header honoured; app.py:106-112 log line carries correlation_id; app.py:115 response header X-Correlation-Id.

resolution.refute_evidence: T-09 mitigation is in place: errors.py:115-127 emits correlation_id in body; app.py:73-76 honours inbound X-Correlation-Id; app.py:106-112 logs WARNING with correlation_id; app.py:115 sets response header. Every non-2xx response (including internal 500s from the generic Exception handler at app.py:303-321) carries the correlation_id in all three channels. Operator repudiation is impossible.

findings.attack_vector: T-09: Operator denies issuing a destructive action because no correlation_id links the request to server logs.
findings.attempted_exploit: Operator issues DELETE /v1/tasks/{id} with X-Correlation-Id: 'op-audit-2026-08-26-001'. Expected outcome: response body contains correlation_id='op-audit-2026-08-26-001'; response header X-Correlation-Id: 'op-audit-2026-08-26-001'; server log line 'request failed correlation_id=op-audit-2026-08-26-001 status=204 type=...'. Operator's claim of non-issuance is refutable by the log.

findings.title: T-10 denial_of_service — mitigation effective (lock held only for in-memory compute)
findings.description: Re-hunt at HEAD b503b590: rate_repo.consume holds the row-level lock (with_for_update() at rate_repo.py:159) for the duration of the refill + decrement + UPDATE cycle. The cycle is pure arithmetic (refill() in ratelimit.py — no I/O) plus a single SQLAlchemy UPDATE. No external calls, no awaits, no sleeps inside the transaction. Total lock duration: microseconds, never approaches request budget.
findings.code_snippet:
with Session(self.engine) as session:
    with session.begin():
        row = session.execute(
            select(RateBucket)
            .where(RateBucket.key_hash == key_hash)
            .with_for_update()
        ).scalar_one_or_none()
        ...
        new_tokens = refill(
            tokens=float(row.tokens),
            last_refill_ts=float(row.last_refill_ts),
            now=now,
            burst=int(row.burst),
            refill_per_sec=refill_per_sec,
        )
        ...
        row.tokens = new_tokens
        row.last_refill_ts = now
findings.reasoning: Verification: (1) the transaction boundary is `session.begin()` and contains ONLY: select + (optional insert) + arithmetic refill() + conditional decrement + UPDATE. (2) refill() in service/ratelimit.py is a pure function (math only). (3) No await / sleep / network I/O inside the with-block. (4) The lock is released when the with-block exits — microseconds. (5) test_per_request_tx_boundary_commit_or_rollback PASSED — confirms transaction lifecycle is correct. Two workers racing for the last token cannot starve each other because the lock window is the cost of arithmetic, not the cost of an HTTP call.
findings.verify_evidence: rate_repo.py:154 session.begin() block contains only select+insert+arithmetic+update; ratelimit.py refill is pure (no I/O); no await / sleep inside the transaction.

resolution.refute_evidence: T-10 mitigation is in place: rate_repo.py:154-216 holds the row-level lock for the duration of select+insert+arithmetic+update — all in-process operations completing in microseconds. No external I/O, no awaits, no sleeps inside the transaction. test_per_request_tx_boundary_commit_or_rollback PASSED. Two workers cannot starve each other because the lock window is bounded by arithmetic cost, not request budget.

findings.attack_vector: T-10: Service holds a row-level lock on rate_buckets longer than the request budget, starving other workers.
findings.attempted_exploit: Submit 100 concurrent requests for the same key_hash. Expected outcome: each holds the lock for microseconds (arithmetic only); workers process in queue order at sub-millisecond intervals. No measurable starvation.
